prompt: Match each person with the direction of growth they agreed with Renata.

pairs.left: Paula takes over calendar sync as well as reminders
Fábio leads the next database investigations
Diego writes up his retry design for all of engineering

prompt: Why does the lesson say a manager who talks about growth only in terms of levels has little to offer?
hint: How often does a level change?

choices.text: Levels are not real
choices.why: They are real and written down; they just change rarely.

choices.text: Engineers do not care about levels
choices.why: Many do; the problem is frequency.

choices.text: Promotions are decided by the panel
choices.why: True, but not the reason given.

choices.text: Promotions come a handful of times in a career, so most people are not near one most of the year
choices.why: Right: between promotions there is still scope, depth and visibility to grow in.

prompt: What does depth need from the manager, by the lesson?

choices.text: A new title
choices.why: Depth is growth at the same level.

choices.text: Public recognition at every demo
choices.why: Fábio dislikes attention; depth is about the problems, not the audience.

choices.text: Fewer on-call shifts
choices.why: Not mentioned as what depth needs.

choices.text: A supply of hard problems in that area, routed to the person
choices.why: Right: depth grows on hard problems, and the manager decides where they go.

prompt: Why did Renata suggest Diego write up existing work rather than change what he worked on?
hint: His case lacked influence beyond Agenda.

choices.text: His work was not good enough
choices.why: The panel praised his technical depth; the gap was visibility.

choices.text: Write-ups are faster than projects
choices.why: Speed was not the reason.

choices.text: Work nobody outside the team has seen cannot count beyond the team
choices.why: Right: the same work, made visible, becomes evidence of influence.

choices.text: Because the architecture review requires one presentation a year from each senior engineer at Caju
choices.why: No such requirement appears.

prompt: An engineer with a newborn tells Renata she wants her job to stay the same size for the next six months. What does the lesson say?
hint: A person can want none of them.

choices.text: That is a legitimate answer, and pushing growth on her would not help
choices.why: Right: stability is a valid choice for a period.

choices.text: Renata should assign a small stretch anyway
choices.why: That ignores what she asked for.

choices.text: It counts against her next promotion case
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson penalises a period of stability.

choices.text: She should move to part-time
choices.why: Not suggested anywhere.

prompt: Who named glue work, and in what?

choices.text: Tanya Reilly
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Will Larson, in Staff Engineer
choices.why: Larson’s book gives the four staff shapes, not the term glue work.

choices.text: Kim Scott, in Radical Candor
choices.why: Scott’s book is about caring and challenging.

choices.text: Andy Grove, in High Output Management, when describing what makes a manager’s output
choices.why: Grove gave the output sum, not this term.

prompt: Which of these are glue work, in the lesson’s sense? Choose all that apply.
hint: Keeps the team functioning; appears in nobody’s list.

choices.text: Presenting at the architecture review
choices.why: No: that is visibility, and it is seen by definition.

choices.text: Noticing that two people are building the same thing
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Shipping the feature on the roadmap
choices.why: No: that is the work glue makes possible, and it is counted.

choices.text: Onboarding a new hire
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Keeping the runbooks current
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Paula onboarded Thiago, and he shipped in his first week. How does the lesson suggest describing that in her record?

choices.text: As “helping out”
choices.why: “Helped with” is one of the weak phrases from lesson 12.

choices.text: It should not be in her record, since onboarding is part of each engineer’s normal duties
choices.why: Leaving it out is exactly how glue work holds people back.

choices.text: As influence: she raised a teammate’s work, with the effect stated
choices.why: Right: glue work written with its effect against the influence row becomes evidence.

choices.text: As craft
choices.why: Craft is about the quality of her own work; this is about others’ work.

prompt: What does the lesson mean by saying glue work is not invisible but undescribed?
hint: Who is best placed to describe it?

choices.text: Nobody wrote it down
choices.why: Right: the manager is best placed to describe it, with its effect.

choices.text: Nobody does it
choices.why: Somebody always does it, often the same person.

choices.text: It should be done in secret
choices.why: Nothing suggests that.

choices.text: It belongs in a separate document from the rest of the person’s work, kept by the people team
choices.why: The point is to put it in the same record, as evidence.

prompt: Put Renata’s three sizing questions for a stretch assignment in order.
items: What is the one new thing?
What happens if it goes wrong?

prompt: Leading a first project, in an unfamiliar codebase, with another department, on a fixed date. What does the lesson call that?

choices.text: A well-sized stretch, since a senior person should be able to handle several unknowns at once
choices.why: The lesson sizes it by the number of new things, and four is too many for a first time.

choices.text: Glue work
choices.why: It is a project, not glue work.

choices.text: A gamble
choices.why: Right: a stretch adds one significant unfamiliar element; this adds several.

choices.text: Depth
choices.why: It stretches several ways at once, not deeper in one area.

prompt: Why did Renata arrange for Thiago to ask Yara anything during his first project?
hint: A safe place to say something.

choices.text: Renata was too busy
choices.why: She set the checkpoints herself; this is about a different kind of support.

choices.text: Yara was going to take over the project if Thiago struggled with any part of it
choices.why: That would be the rescue the lesson warns against.

choices.text: He needed somewhere to say “I don’t know how” that was not his manager
choices.why: Right: the manager is rarely the safe place for that sentence.

choices.text: To give Yara visibility
choices.why: Not the reason given.

prompt: A stretch with no conversation afterwards is just a hard ___.

A team’s manager notices that one engineer runs every retrospective, writes every postmortem and onboards every new hire, while her promotion case keeps failing for “not enough technical depth”. What does this lesson suggest first?

choices.text: Tell her to stop doing glue work immediately
choices.why: The team still needs it done; the fix is to share it and count it.

choices.text: Agree with the panel
choices.why: The panel may be right about depth, but the record is missing half the picture.

choices.text: Move her into management, since glue work is what managers do
choices.why: Some people want that path; it should not be the default for being good at glue.

choices.text: Rotate the glue work, and record what she did with its effect against the ladder
choices.why: Right: spread the tax, and describe the work so it counts as evidence of influence.
